Scope: refresh four Tier-1 projects, rank open contribution opportunities, pick ONE.

## AI-contribution policy (hard filter)

| Project | Verdict | Exact source |
|---|---|---|
| Jan | SILENT (allowed by default; we disclose anyway) | Checked at 14a7206: CONTRIBUTING.md, src-tauri/CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/pull_request_template.md, no CODE_OF_CONDUCT/AGENTS/CLAUDE file at root. No AI line in any. Local norm: maintainers and contributors disclose AI use in comments (e.g. janhq/jan#8743 comment by Jokasa7, "Disclosure: I used AI-assisted code search"). |
| OpenHands app | Allowed, with a human section | OpenHands/AGENTS.md:49 "The `HUMAN:` section in PR descriptions is reserved for human contributors only. AI agents must not add to, edit, move, or remove it." PR template (.github/pull_request_template.md:3-5, 8-15): AGENT section needs evidence the code "runs properly end-to-end. Just running unit tests is NOT sufficient." Prepared text must leave HUMAN for Drake. |
| OpenHands SDK | Same pattern | software-agent-sdk/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:3-5 and :12 "AI agents: you must not edit this section."; :18-22 end-to-end evidence required. |
| goose | Allowed, no disclosure needed | goose/CONTRIBUTING.md:80-83 "There's no need to tell us you used AI in your work... you are responsible for the final code... We'll close any vibe coded submissions that obviously skip this step." (We disclose anyway.) |
| Open Interpreter | SILENT on AI; routes core changes to Codex | open-interpreter/.github/pull_request_template.md "We generally do not accept changes to core Codex behavior in this repository." No AI line found in AGENTS.md, template, or CONTRIBUTING (none exists). |

Nobody forbids AI-assisted work. Every prepared PR text discloses AI assistance regardless.

## Competition method
For each finalist: `gh issue view` (assignees, comments), GraphQL `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, `linkedBranches`, `timelineItems(CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT)`, and `gh pr list --state all --search <n>`. Run 2026-10-04.
Finding: the OpenHands repos and goose are saturated; most low-risk bugs have 1-4 competing open PRs, many from AI-driven accounts.

Components: Impact, Repro (on this aarch64 headless box, no GPU for now), Review (small, testable), Rel (INTERPLANE relevance), Need (maintainer demand), Comp (competition penalty), Scope (scope-risk penalty).

Reasons (one line each):
1. #8975: pure function `assemble_tool_array` (src-tauri/src/core/agent/upstream.rs:919) pushes both tools and keeps one map entry; an existing test already asserts the duplicate (advertised names `["search","search"]`); fully headless, no model. Comp 2: no linked PR or branch (GraphQL), no assignee, but commenter DeepanshuPal (2026-09-27) offered to "take the fix once you pick" and the issue author thinhlpg is active on the epic #8956. Scope 2: issue lists three options and says "Not decided here".
2. #8743: only one reporter (macOS, LM Studio); Jokasa7's trace of web-app/src/lib/custom-chat-transport.ts (refreshTools :963, shouldEnableTools :1521-1523) found no code path that drops tools; maintainers asked for logs 2026-08-29, no reply. Reproduction on source is not possible yet (hypothesized capability-persistence or list_tools timing). Comp 1: no PR; cross-referenced only by #8793.
3. SDK #5458: open PR #5468 (2026-10-03) already covers it.
4. SDK #4965: open PR #4981 (2026-09-12) covers it; OpenHands template needs end-to-end evidence (likely needs inference).
5. SDK #5354: open PR #5355 covers it.
6. goose #12544: feature-shaped, needs a live llama.cpp.
7. goose #12533: PR #12534 open.
8. goose #12449: design problem across ACP sessions, no repro recipe.
9. OI #1938: Windows desktop app plus Ollama inference; OI PR template routes core Codex behavior to openai/codex.

Not scored (assigned or has PRs, so out per rule 4): goose #12590, #12556, #12513, #12598, #12669 (all have assignees); OpenHands app #17733 (PR #17735), #17748 (PR #17749), #16978 (4 PRs), #17803 (maintainer drafts SDK#5382/#5383); SDK #5290 (PR #5291).

## INTERPLANE relevance map
- #8975: Lenshift/Crossveil style invariant (one name, one target, one definition on the wire), Probe fixture.
- #8743: capability advertisement must survive provider routing (Lenshift, Probe).
- #4965 / #5354: wire-shape validity for strict providers (Crossveil), tool-call batch integrity (RelayLine).

## Pick
Jan #8975. Reason: only candidate that is unclaimed by any PR, reproducible headless without a model, in the preferred project, and generically valuable. Risks named above (soft interest by DeepanshuPal; design choice left to maintainers). #8743 stays the mission-named follow-up if more reporter data appears.
No qualification/ecosystems/ entry is added: no real test evidence against an INTERPLANE build exists yet.
